hypothesis: The mixed|balanced|normal state tilt on the accepted consensus sleeve (exp-20260612-018: +7.4% aggregate EV, zero regression, improved drawdown, rejected only on APP single-ticker concentration) becomes acceptable when the tilt carries a per-ticker repetition cap: only a ticker's first N in-cell entries within a trailing 60-trading-day window receive the 1.5x paper notional tilt, diluting single-name dependence below the 50% concentration guard.
causal_components: per-ticker trailing-60d tilt cap N in 2 or 3

prediction.confidence_reason: Mechanism: exp-20260612-018 proved the state-conditioned tilt direction (EV/PnL/drawdown all improved, zero window regression) and failed solely because APP carries 51.4% of in-cell positive PnL, a scalar-invariant property. Capping tilt at a ticker's first N in-cell entries per trailing 60 trading days removes most APP/MU repetition (11 and 8 in-cell rows) while keeping the diversified majority tilted, so the incremental PnL share should drop well below 50%. Main disconfirmers: APP rows may be the bulk of the cell's positive PnL so even capped exposure could keep the in-cell share above 50%; capping shrinks tilted rows to roughly 21-26 so the EV lift may thin out; and the cell remains in-sample-screened, capping any pass at accepted_paper_pending_forward.

calibration.surprise_note: The cap backfired directionally: APP's in-cell entries are temporally dispersed (re-qualifying across months, so a trailing-60-trading-day repetition cap rarely binds it) while diversifier names like MU cluster within one window and got capped hard, so both concentration shares ROSE (in-cell 51.4%->52.8%/53.2%, incremental 56.0%/58.6%). The cell's apparent regime edge is substantially a persistent single-name (APP) effect, not a fixable weighting artifact.
